title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 59 (Rectification of Register of Members)

content.overview: Section 59 allows an aggrieved person, any member or the company to seek rectification for an entry/omission without sufficient cause or default/unnecessary delay; it also addresses certain unlawful transfers and depository records.
content.glance: Section 59 allows an aggrieved person, any member or the company to seek rectification for an entry/omission without sufficient cause or default/unnecessary delay; it also addresses certain unlawful transfers and depository records.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 59 (Rectification of register of members). Where a person's name is entered in or omitted from the register of members without sufficient cause, or default or unnecessary delay occurs in recording a person becoming or ceasing to be a member, the aggrieved person, any member or the company may apply to the Tribunal. The section also provides for a competent court outside India specified by Central Government notification in relation to foreign members or debenture-holders residing outside India. After hearing the parties, the Tribunal may dismiss the application, direct registration of a transfer or transmission within ten days of receipt of the order, or direct rectification of the register or depository records and award damages sustained by the aggrieved party. The section preserves the right to transfer securities and voting rights unless suspended by Tribunal order. Where a transfer contravenes the SCRA, SEBI Act, Companies Act or another law, specified applicants may seek directions to correct the contravention and rectify records. Subsection (5) was omitted with effect from 21 December 2020; do not repeat its former penalty as current law. This is distinct from section 58 appeals against refusal to register.

sections.heading: Grounds and standing
sections.body: A person aggrieved, any member or the company may apply where a name is entered or omitted without sufficient cause, or default/unnecessary delay occurs in recording a person becoming or ceasing to be a member. The section also provides for a competent court outside India specified by Central Government notification in relation to foreign members or debenture-holders residing outside India.

sections.heading: Orders under subsection (2)
sections.body: After hearing the parties, the Tribunal may dismiss the application, direct the company to register the transfer or transmission within ten days of receipt of the order, or direct rectification of the register/depository records and award damages sustained by the aggrieved party.

sections.heading: Transfer rights and voting
sections.body: Section 59 does not restrict a holder's right to transfer securities. A person acquiring securities is entitled to voting rights unless the Tribunal has suspended those rights by order.

sections.heading: Contravention of securities law
sections.body: Where a transfer contravenes the SCRA, SEBI Act, Companies Act or another law, the Tribunal may, on an application by the depository, company, depository participant, holder of securities or SEBI, direct the company/depository to correct the contravention and rectify its register or records.

sections.heading: Current penalty status
sections.body: Subsection (5) was omitted with effect from 21 December 2020. Do not state the former subsection (5) penalty as current law.

examples.title: Wrongful omission
examples.body: A transferee’s name is omitted from the register without sufficient cause. The transferee applies under s. 59 for rectification and damages.

examples.title: Delay in registration
examples.body: Unnecessary delay in entering a transmission on death leads the legal representative to seek rectification under s. 59.

hypotheticals.question: A person's name is omitted from the register without sufficient cause. What remedy may section 59 provide?
hypotheticals.analysis: The aggrieved person, any member or the company may apply to the Tribunal. After hearing the parties, the Tribunal may direct registration, rectify the register/depository records and award damages sustained by the aggrieved party.

hypotheticals.question: A transfer is alleged to contravene securities legislation. What route should be considered?
hypotheticals.analysis: Subsection (4) addresses transfers in contravention of the SCRA, SEBI Act, Companies Act or another law, and identifies applicants who may seek directions to correct the contravention and rectify records.

distinctions.left: Section 59 addresses wrongful entry/omission, default or unnecessary delay and certain statutory contraventions.
distinctions.right: Section 58 addresses refusal to register transfer/transmission and the relevant appeal route.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming only the company may seek rectification.
misconceptions.correction: The person aggrieved, any member or the company may apply under subsection (1).

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the distinct orders available under section 59.
misconceptions.correction: The Tribunal may direct registration of transfer/transmission, rectify the register or depository records, and award damages where permitted.

misconceptions.trap: Quoting the former subsection (5) penalty as current law.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (5) was omitted effective 21 December 2020; its former penalty is not a current section 59 penalty.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Who may apply under section 59(1)?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The person aggrieved, any member of the company, or the company; a specified competent court outside India may be relevant for foreign members/debenture-holders residing outside India.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What may the Tribunal order?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It may dismiss the application, direct registration within ten days of receipt of the order, or direct rectification and award damages sustained by the aggrieved party.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is the former subsection (5) penalty still part of section 59?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Subsection (5) was omitted with effect from 21 December 2020.
